messages:
maya: quick FYI — opened PR 4123 to add a compatibility note for the new edge-quant variants. i documented max_tokens and the CPU-fallback behavior but not 100% confident about the exact limits for 8-bit quant + prefix cache. can someone from eng-ml confirm?

alex: thanks. can you paste the snippet you added for the SDK (streaming + fallback)? want to make sure it's idiomatic.

maya: sure — in the PR I added this example for python streaming fallback:

```
from redwood import Client
c = Client()
# prefer edge-quant, but fall back to cpu-compat if not available
resp = c.generate(model="edge-quant-7b", streaming=True, fallback=["cpu-compat-7b"], max_tokens=512)
for chunk in resp.stream():
    print(chunk.text, end="")
```

alex: minor nit — our SDK currently expects `fallback` to be a single string or empty list, not a list-of-strings. want to avoid implying multi-fallback is supported until runtime routing lands. change to `fallback="cpu-compat-7b"`?

simon: also we should be explicit that prefix caching is disabled when falling back to cpu runtime (due to KV layout differences). otherwise users will assume same throughput. maya, can you add a small note in the limits table row?

maya: good point. i will add: "Prefix/KV cache not preserved on CPU fallback; expect increased token latency and no cache hit rate." done in draft, pushing update.

docs-bot: Assigned reviewers: @alex, @simon. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123

eva: another user-facing thing — the model-catalog table shows `context_window` as 8k for edge-quant-7b. is that enforced on CPU fallback? should probably show "8k (hosted only) / 4k (cpu-fallback)" or similar to avoid confusion.

alex: yes, let's be explicit. we should also add a brief benchmark note: on cpu-fallback 4k runs at ~0.6 tokens/sec on a single vCPU (internal benchmark). put that under the "benchmarks" column as a one-line caveat.

maya: added the 4k/8k split and the micro-benchmark note. can someone sanity-check the phrasing: "Context window: 8k on edge-quant runtime; when routed to CPU-compat fallback, max effective context is 4k (KV split + memory constraints)."

simon: phrasing LGTM. recommend adding a tiny table cell: "Streaming behavior: SSE streaming supported on edge-quant; CPU fallback returns chunked non-SSE responses (no server-sent events)." that's important for client SDKs.

maya: added that too. also fixed two broken links in the model-card: the runtime behavior link went to an older doc — replaced with /docs/runtime-fallbacks.md.

alex: perfect. one last check — can you update the SDK snippet in the examples directory (docs/examples/sdk/streaming-fallback.py) so it matches the single-fallback signature? reviewers will ping on that.

maya: updating file now. push in 2 mins. ping me if CI on docs site shows rendering errors.

docs-bot: CI: docs build queued.

alex: thanks — will review once CI passes. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all. tagging @simon again in the PR comments to confirm the cache note is accurate.
